safi-cedvel:70-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction, (ألقي) a passive past verb, (السحرة) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative, (سجّدا) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial), (بربّ) attached to (آمنّا).
Clause: «ألقي السحرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.:
فألقى موسى عصاه فتلقّفت كلّ ما صنعوا فألقي السحرة ... (Moses cast down his staff, and it swallowed up all that they had made, and the sorcerers were cast down ...)
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause [Note: It is possible that it is in the position of an accusative ḥāl, with an implied (قد).].
And the clause: «آمنّا ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said (maqūl al-qawl).

* Benefits:
Every hamza that occurs at the beginning of a word, whether with ḍamma, kasra or fatḥa, and that has the interrogative hamza or the vocative hamza prefixed to it, is written, in the word where it now stands in the middle, as a letter homogeneous with its own vowel, as is the view of the majority. In the interrogative, for the hamza with an initial ḍamma you say أألقي. For the one with an initial fatḥa you say أألقي. For the one with an initial kasra you say أئلقاء. [Translator's note: the source prints أألقي for both the ḍamma case and the fatḥa case; it is reproduced as written.] Ibn Mālik said: the hamza is written as an alif, according to its origin, in the interrogative and the vocative, like this:
أأحمد. أألقي أإلقاء. Because it stands in the position of an independent word, and this is the better course and the school of most of the grammarians.
Note: the orthography of the Qur'an is special to it.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(له) attached to (آمنتم), (قبل) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (آمنتم), (لكم) attached to (آذن), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن آذن..) is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct).
(اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis, (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) in the position of a nominative, an adjective (naʿt) of (كبير), (الفاء) resumptive, (اللام) the lām of an oath, for an implied oath, (أقطّعنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and the agent (fāʿil) is "I", (من خلاف) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الأيدي) and (الأرجل), i.e. "differing (limbs)", (الواو) a conjunction, (لأصلّبنّكم) like (لأقطّعنّ), (في جذوع) attached to (أصلّبنّكم), (الواو) a conjunction, (لتعلمنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the retention of the nūn; it was dropped because of the succession of similar letters.. and the (الواو), which was dropped because of the meeting of two silent letters, is the agent, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, (أيّنا) a relative noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative direct object (mafʿūl bihi).. and (نا) is muḍāf ilayhi [Note: it is possible that it is an interrogative noun, a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is (أشدّ), the clause being the object of the verb of knowing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.], (أشدّ) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", (عذابا) a tamyīz (specification), accusative, (أبقى) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (أشدّ), nominative, its sign being the implied ḍamma.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «آمنتم له ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «آذن لكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «إنّه لكبيركم ... » has no grammatical position; causal.
And the clause: «علّمكم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «أقطّعنّ ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.. and the implied oath clause is resumptive.
And the clause: «أصلّبنّكم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the oath's response.
And the clause: «تعلمنّ ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the oath's response.
And the clause: « (هو) أشدّ ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (أيّ).

* Morphology:
(أبقى): an elative (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral بقي, on the pattern أفعل, and it has an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is أبقي, the yāʾ having a vowel after a fatḥa was changed to an alif.

* Rhetoric:
- Simile (tashbīh):
In His words, the Exalted, «وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ».
He likened the firm lodging of the crucified man in the trunk to the firm lodging of a thing contained in its container; hence it was said (فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ).

* Benefits:
1- «آذن».
When two hamzas meet at the beginning of a word, the second hamza turns into a long vowel (madda), in order to ease pronunciation, and this is one of the characteristics of this language, which in all its positions inclines toward ease wherever it can be found.
2- The abundance of emphatic devices in the speech that He, the Exalted, reported on the tongue of Pharaoh is one of the kinds of Qur'anic eloquence; if it indicates anything, it indicates the arrogance and tyranny of the Pharaohs and their excess in unbelief and claims to lordship, as in:
«إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ، فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ، لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ، وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ.. إلخ» (etc.).

safi-cedvel:72-73.t:
* I'rab:
(على ما) attached to (نؤثرك), (من البيّنات) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun (نا), (الواو) a conjunction - or the wāw of the oath - (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the relative (ما) [Note: or in the position of a genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear".], (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis of an implied condition, (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of an accusative direct object (mafʿūl bihi) [Note: al-ʿUkbarī allowed another aspect, namely that it is an adverbial particle, with the object omitted, i.e. "decree your decree".], (قاض) the khabar (predicate) of (أنت), nominative, its sign of nominative being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ), (إنّما) a restrictive particle (kāffa) and the thing it restricts (makfūfa), (هذه) accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in this" [Note: or a direct object whose governor is (تقضي), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "you decree the affairs of this life".. and it is possible that the demonstrative is an adverbial attached to (تقضي), with its object omitted, i.e. "your command" or "your purpose".], (الحياة) a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative, accusative - or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) - (الدينا) an adjective (naʿt) of (الحياة), accusative, its sign of accusative being the implied fatḥa on the alif.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «لن نؤثرك ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «جاءنا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «فطرنا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «اقض ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you wish to punish us, then decree".
And the clause: «أنت قاض ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «تقضي ... » has no grammatical position; causal.
73- (بربّنا) attached to (آمنّا), (اللام) for cause, (يغفر) accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām, (لنا) attached to (يغفر), (الواو) a conjunction, (ما) a relative in the position of an accusative, conjoined to (خطايا) [Note: or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "what you compelled us to do is struck off from us".], (عليه) attached to (أكرهتنا), (من السحر) a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (عليه).
And the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يغفر..) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (آمنّا).
(الواو) a conjunction (أبقى) conjoined to (خير) by the second wāw, nominative, its sign of nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif.
And the clause: «إنّا آمنّا ... » has no grammatical position; another causal resumptive.
And the clause: «آمنّا ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «يغفر ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «أكرهتنا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «الله خير ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the content of what was said.

* Morphology:
(قاض): an active participle from the triliteral قضى, on the pattern فاع; its final lām, the yāʾ, was dropped because of the meeting of two silent letters, the silence of the yāʾ and the silence of the tanwīn.

safi-cedvel:74-76.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّه) the hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the ism of inna, (من) a conditional noun that jusses, indeclinable in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject), (يأت) an imperfect verb, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is "huwa", (مجرما) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (يأت), (الفاء) the connective of an apodosis, (له) attached to an omitted khabar of inna, (جهنّم) the ism of inna, placed later, accusative, (فيها) attached to (يموت).
Clause: «إنّه من ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: it may be a resumptive from Allah the Exalted, and it may be a resumptive from the words of the sorcerers, to confirm the cause of their belief in Moses.].
And the clause: «من يأت ربّه ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «يأت ربّه ... » is in the position of the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it is possible that the khabar is the two clauses, protasis and apodosis together.].
And the clause: «إنّ له جهنّم ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
And the clause: «لا يموت ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun in (له) [Note: and the governor in it is the sense of emphasis.. and it is possible that the clause is an adjective of (جهنّم), in the position of an accusative.].
And the clause: «لا يحيا ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause (لا يموت).
75- (الواو) a conjunction (من يأته مؤمنا) is like (من يأت ربّه مجرما) (قد) a particle of certainty (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar (الدرجات) a mubtadaʾ placed later, nominative.
And the clause: «من يأته ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause (من يأت ربّه).
And the clause: «يأته مؤمنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «قد عمل ... » is in the position of an accusative, a second ḥāl from the agent of (يأت).
And the clause: «أولئك لهم الدرجات ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
And the clause: «لهم الدرجات ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
76- (جنّات) a badal (substitute) for (الدرجات), nominative, (من تحتها) attached to (تجري) [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl from (الأنهار).], (خالدين) an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun in (لهم), and the governor in it is the sense of settlement or the sense of the demonstrative, (فيها) attached to (خالدين), (الواو) resumptive, (ذلك) a mubtadaʾ, (من) a relative in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «تجري ... » is in the position of a nominative, an adjective (naʿt) of (جنّات).
And the clause: «ذلك جزاء ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «تزكّى ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(يحيا): it is written in the Mushaf with the form of the yāʾ, (يحيى), while the rule of orthography says it is written with the form of the long alif.
(تزكّى): it has an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is تزكّي: the yāʾ, having a vowel after a fatḥa, was changed to an alif. The origin of the lām in the verb is a wāw, because it is from زكا يزكو.

safi-cedvel:77-77.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (اللام) the lām of an oath, for an implied oath, (قد) a particle of certainty, (إلى موسى) attached to (أوحينا), (أن) explicative, (بعبادي) attached to (أسر), (الفاء) a conjunction, (لهم) attached to (اضرب) [Note: or attached to an omitted second direct object, since (اضرب) is given the sense of "make".], (في البحر) attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (طريقا), (يبسا) a second adjective of (طريقا), accusative.
Clause: «أوحينا ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.. and the oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
And the clause: «أسر ... » has no grammatical position; explicative.
And the clause: «اضرب ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the explicative clause.
And the clause: «لا تخاف ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of (اضرب) [Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
And the clause: «لا تخشى ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause (لا تخاف).

* Morphology:
(يبسا): it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral يبس, of the pattern of فرح, and it is used as a description for the sake of intensification or on the basis of an omitted muḍāf.. and it is possible that it is the plural of يابس, like خادم and خدم, used to describe a singular for intensification; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(دركا): a noun with the meaning of the "overtaking", i.e. catching up.. its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
1- Rational trope (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī):
In His words, the Exalted, «فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقاً فِي الْبَحْرِ»: the original is "strike the sea so that it becomes a path for them".
2- Synecdochic/relational trope (al-majāz al-mursal):
In His words, the Exalted, «يَبَساً».
It was not "dry" when Allah the Exalted addressed him, but it is by consideration of what it would become, like His words, the Exalted, «إِنِّي أَرانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْراً».

safi-cedvel:78-78.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction, (بجنوده) attached to a ḥāl from Pharaoh [Note: or attached to (أتبعهم), the bāʾ being for transitivity.], (الفاء) a conjunction, (من اليمّ) attached to (غشيهم), (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative, the agent of (غشيهم), and the agent of the second (غشيهم) is a pronoun referring back to (ما).
Clause: «أتبعهم فرعون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive, i.e. "so Moses did what he was commanded, and Pharaoh pursued them ..".
And the clause: «غشيهم ... ما» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (أتبعهم).
And the clause: «غشيهم (the second) ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).

* Rhetoric:
- Magnification of terror (al-tahwīl):
In His words, the Exalted, «فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ ما غَشِيَهُمْ»:
that is, it rose over them from it, and it covered them with what covered them, of the dreadful matter whose measure cannot be gauged and whose essence cannot be reached; for the basis of terrifying and magnifying is that it goes beyond the limits of understanding and description, not the hearing of the story.

safi-cedvel:79-79.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (ما) negative.
Clause: «أضلّ فرعون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما هدى ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Rhetoric:
1- Mockery (al-tahakkum) in His words, the Exalted, «وَما هَدى». Mockery is that one brings an expression while the intended meaning is the opposite of what it requires, like their saying «إِنَّكَ لَأَنْتَ الْحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ»; its purpose is to put him in the opposite of these two states.
The clarification of the meaning of mockery: His words, the Exalted, «وَما هَدى» are of the type of allusion (talmīḥ), and are a reference to the accursed one's claim to guide the people in His words, the Exalted, «وَما أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ الرَّشادِ». He is like one who made a claim and exaggerated it, and when its time came and he did not bring it about, it was said to him: "you have not brought what you claimed", in mockery and ridicule.

safi-cedvel:80-81.t:
* I'rab:
(بني) a vocative muḍāf, accusative, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ, for it is attached to the sound masculine plural, (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote, (قد) a particle of certainty, (من عدوّكم) attached to (أنجيناكم), (جانب) a second direct object, accusative, by an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "coming to the side of the Mount" [Note: or it is an adverbial of (واعدناكم), and the second object is omitted, i.e. "We appointed you to come to the side".], (عليكم) attached to (نزّلنا).
The vocative clause: «يا بني ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «أنجيناكم ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «واعدناكم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the vocative's response.
And the clause: «نزّلنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the vocative's response.
81- (من طيّبات) attached to (كلوا), (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi [Note: and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) of the relative is omitted, i.e. "with it".. and it is possible that it is a maṣdar particle, the interpreted maṣdar being muḍāf ilayhi.], (الواو) a conjunction, (لا) a prohibitive that jusses, (فيه) attached to (تطغوا), (الفاء) the fāʾ of causality, (يحلّ) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the fāʾ, (عليكم) attached to (يحلّ), (غضبي) the agent, nominative, its sign of nominative being the implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يحلّ..) is conjoined to a maṣdar drawn from the preceding prohibition, i.e.: "let there be no transgression on your part in provision, so that there follows the descent of wrath from Allah".
(الواو) resumptive, (من) a conditional noun that jusses, indeclinable in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ, (عليه) attached to (يحلل), the protasis, (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis.
And the clause: «كلوا ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumptive.
And the clause: «رزقناكم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «لا تطغوا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (كلوا)..
And the clause: «يحلّ.. غضبي ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «من يحلل عليه غضبي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يحلل ... غضبي» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «قد هوى ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(هوى): its imperfect is يهوي - with a yāʾ at the end - so it has an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is هوي - with a yāʾ at the end - the yāʾ, having a vowel after a fatḥa, was changed to an alif.

* Rhetoric:
1- Rational trope (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī):
In His words, the Exalted, «وَواعَدْناكُمْ»:
the attribution of the appointment to them, although it was for Moses, peace be upon him, in view of its association with them and the spread of its benefit to them, as if all of them were parties to the appointment; so the trope lies in the attribution. In that there is the due fulfilment of the setting of reminding of favour.
2- Metaphor (istiʿāra):
In His words, the Exalted, «فَقَدْ هَوى»:
He borrowed the word "falling" (hawā), which is dropping from a height to a low place, for destruction and ruin.

safi-cedvel:82-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis, (لمن) attached to (غفّار), (صالحا) a direct object, accusative.
Clause: «إنّي لغفّار ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «تاب ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «آمن ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «عمل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «اهتدى» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (عمل صالحا).

* Benefits:
- The exodus of the Children of Israel from Egypt:
"The day grew bright, and the Children of Israel distinguished right guidance from error, and they turned to the noble Messenger of Allah. How could their insights not open, when they had touched the sign of truth, radiant and shining, and their eyes were cooled by it; and they sought to flee from the land of the Copts, seeking safety and distance from the wrongdoing people.
Moses led them on at the beginning of the night, hastening, driven by fear and protected by faith, until they stood before the sea, and dismay took hold of them. Then Joshua son of Nūn cried out: 'O one who spoke with Allah, the sea is before us and the enemy behind us.' So Allah revealed to Moses to strike the sea with his staff; he struck it, and behold, there were twelve paths for twelve tribes.
And this is the confirmation of His words, the Exalted:
«فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقاً فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَساً لا تَخافُ دَرَكاً وَلا تَخْشى».
The tribes of the lineages hurried to the shore of safety and peace, while the water stood on both sides of every path like a mighty mountain, until they crossed in safety.
Pharaoh came on with his soldiers, and they entered those paths in the sea; and when they were in the middle of it, it closed over them and drowned them all, and they became an example for those after them. At this critical moment Pharaoh believed and said:
«آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنو إسرائيل»."

safi-cedvel:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (ما) an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ in the position of a nominative, (عن قومك) attached to (أعجلك), (موسى) a vocative, a single proper noun, indeclinable on the implied ḍamma.
Clause: «أعجلك ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of an implied saying, i.e. "We said to him".
And the clause: «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical.

safi-cedvel:84-84.t:
* I'rab:
(هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ, (أولاء) a demonstrative noun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative khabar [Note: al-ʿUkbarī allowed that (أولاء) is a relative and (على أثري) its ṣila, which is remote.], (على أثري) attached to an omitted second khabar, i.e. "coming" [Note: or it is a ḥāl from an implied element, i.e. "they are coming upon my trail".], (إليك) attached to (عجلت), (ربّ) a vocative muḍāf, accusative, its sign of accusative being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, which is omitted for lightness, and the (الياء) omitted for lightness is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), (اللام) for cause, (ترضى) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām, its sign of accusative being the implied fatḥa, and the agent is "you".
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن ترضى) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (عجلت).
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumptive.
And the clause: «هم أولاء ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «عجلت ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of what was said.
And the clause: «ربّ ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical, for the sake of seeking mercy.
And the clause: «ترضى ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(أثري): a noun that has the sense of an adverbial, i.e. "after me".. its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:85-85.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) causal, (من بعدك) attached to (فتنّا), (الواو) a conjunction - or a circumstantial wāw - Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّا قد فتنّا ... » has no grammatical position; a cause for an implied content of what was said, i.e. "do not wait for your people, for We have tried them".
And the clause: «قد فتنّا ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «أضلّهم السامريّ» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إنّا قد فتنّا» [Note: or in the position of an accusative ḥāl, with an implied (قد).].

* Morphology:
(السامريّ): a relational noun (ism mansūb) attributed to Sāmira, a tribe of the Children of Israel, and his name was Mūsā ibn Ẓafar.

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive, (إلى قومه) attached to (رجع), (غضبان) an accusative ḥāl from Moses, and it is barred from tanwīn because it is an adjective on the pattern فعلان, (أسفا) a second accusative ḥāl, (قوم) a vocative muḍāf, accusative, its sign of accusative being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ, omitted for lightness, and the omitted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi, (الهمزة) for the interrogative of rebuke, (وعدا) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative, confirming the verb [Note: or a direct object, accusative, if it is in the sense of "that which is promised".], (الهمزة) for the interrogative, (الفاء) a conjunction, (عليكم) attached to (طال), (أم) a conjunction equivalent to the hamza, (عليكم) the second, attached to (يحلّ), (من ربّكم) attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (غضب), (الفاء) a conjunction, (موعدي) a direct object, accusative, its sign of accusative being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, and the (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «رجع موسى ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumptive.
And the clause: «النداء: يا قوم ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «يعدكم ربّكم ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «طال.. العهد ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the vocative's response.
And the clause: «أردتم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (طال) ...
And the clause: «يحلّ.. غضب ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يحلّ..) is in the position of an accusative direct object, its governor being (أردتم).
And the clause: «أخلفتم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (أردتم).

* Benefits:
- The appointment of Moses: Moses chose seventy men from his people and set out for the appointed time of his Lord, to receive from Him a book that would be the first and last reference for the Children of Israel. He arrived after thirty days, and it was revealed to him to complete them to forty. Moses was made happy by his nearness to his Lord and received His message from Him; and when he asked to see Him, He said to him: "Look at the mountain; if it stays in its place, then you will see Me." When he looked at the mountain, the mountain crumbled and sank into the earth, and Moses fell down senseless; and when he recovered he rose glorifying Allah, the Great, the Most High.
And when Moses came back with the tablets that contain his law, Allah revealed to him: «يا موسى، إني اصطفيتك على الناس برسالاتي وبكلامي، فخذ ما آتيتك وكن من الشاكرين».

safi-cedvel:87-88.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative, (بملكنا) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (أخلفنا) [Note: or attached to (أخلفنا), the bāʾ being causal.], (الواو) a conjunction, (لكنّا) a particle of correction (istidrāk) that governs the accusative, and (نا) is the pronoun, the ism of lakinna, (حمّلنا) a passive past verb.. and (نا) is the pronoun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), (أوزارا) a direct object, accusative, (من زينة) attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (أوزارا), (الفاء) the first is a conjunction, and the second is resumptive, (كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), its governor being (ألقى).
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما أخلفنا ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «لكنّا حمّلنا ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of what was said.
And the clause: «حمّلنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of lakinna.
And the clause: «قذفناها ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause (حمّلنا).
And the clause: «ألقى السامريّ ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
88- (الفاء) a conjunction, (لهم) attached to (أخرج), (جسدا) an adjective (naʿt) of (عجلا), accusative, (له) attached to a fronted khabar, (خوار) a mubtadaʾ placed later, nominative, (الفاء) a conjunction in both places, and the agent of (نسي) is a pronoun referring back to Moses, peace be upon him, i.e. "Moses forgot his Lord here - and he is the calf - and went off to seek him on the mountain".
And the clause: «أخرج ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «ألقى السامريّ».
And the clause: «له خوار ... » is in the position of an accusative, a second adjective of (عجلا) [Note: or a ḥāl from the calf, since the indefinite has been described.].
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (أخرج).
And the clause: «هذا إلهكم ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «نسي ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of what was said.

* Morphology:
(ملكنا): a maṣdar of ملك in the sense of "he was able", on the pattern فعل with a fatḥa and a sukūn.

safi-cedvel:89-89.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of rebuke, (الفاء) resumptive [Note: because the people's account ended at His words (فنسي), and the speech is a fresh start from Allah.], (لا) negative, (أن) the lightened form of the heavy (أنّ), and its ism is an omitted ḍamīr al-shaʾn, (لا) negative, and the agent of (يرجع) is a pronoun referring back to the calf, (إليهم) attached to (يرجع), (قولا) a direct object, accusative, (الواو) a conjunction, (لهم) attached to an omitted ḥāl from (ضرّا), (لا) the second is redundant (zāʾida), to confirm the negation, (نفعا) conjoined to (ضرّا), accusative.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ألّا يرجع ... ) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of (يرون).
Clause: «يرون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يرجع ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the operative lightened (أن).
And the clause: «يملك ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause (يرجع).

safi-cedvel:90-90.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (اللام) the lām of an oath, for an implied oath, (قد) a particle of certainty, (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of a genitive, attached to (قال), (يا قوم) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (86) of this sūra.], (إنّما) a restrictive particle (kāffa) and the thing it restricts (makfūfa), (به) attached to (فتنتم), (الواو) a conjunction, (الفاء) the connective of an implied conditional apodosis, and the sign of accusative in (أمري) is the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, and the (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.. the oath clause has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the vocative clause: «يا قوم» is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «فتنتم به ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «إنّ ربّكم الرحمن ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «اتّبعوني ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you believe me, then follow me".

safi-cedvel:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(نبرح) an imperfect incomplete verb (fiʿl nāqiṣ), accusative, its ism a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن" (we), (عليه) attached to the khabar (عاكفين), (حتّى) a particle of limit and genitive, (يرجع) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after (حتّى).. (إلينا) attached to (يرجع).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يرجع) is in the position of a genitive by (حتّى), attached to (عاكفين).
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «لن نبرح ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «يرجع إلينا موسى» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative; (عليك) attached to (أنزلنا); (اللام) for causation; (تشقى) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif, and the fāʿil (agent) is أنت (you).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تشقى) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أنزلنا).
(إلّا) for a disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) exception, with the meaning of لكن (but); (تذكرة) a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) whose governor is implied, i.e. "We sent it down as a reminder" «[Note: it comes here in the accusative because its agent agrees with the agent of the verb and refers to Allah; whereas in (لتشقى) the preposition was used because the agent of the maṣdar — referring to the Messenger — differs from the agent of the sending down, which refers to Allah.. It is also possible that (تذكرة) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, as it is possible that it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "as a reminder for whoever fears".]»; (لمن) attached to (تذكرة); (تنزيلا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, its implied form being "نزّلناه"; (من) attached to (تنزيل) because it stands in for its verb; (العلا) an naʿt (adjective) of السموات, accusative, its sign of the accusative being an implied fatḥa.
The clause «ما أنزلنا ...» has no grammatical position; inceptive.
The clause «تشقى ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يخشى ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(تشقى): it has a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is تشقي with a yāʾ; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.
(تذكرة): a samāʿī (heard-pattern) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb ذكّر, whose regular form is تذكير; the tāʾ marbūṭa at its end was given in exchange for the yāʾ, for lightening; its pattern is تفعلة.
(يخشى): it has a weak-letter change by conversion; its origin is يخشي; the yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.
(العلا): the plural of عليا, the feminine of أعلى.. it is on the form of preference, أفعل, but pure description is intended by it, i.e. "the high"; the pattern of عليا is فعلى with ḍamma then sukūn, and the pattern of العلا is فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa. It is also permissible to write the short alif in the form of the undotted yāʾ (العلى), because with the triliteral wāw-type whose first radical has ḍamma, two ways of writing the alif are valid: the first is writing the long alif according to the general rule, and the second is writing the short alif according to the opinion of the Kufans and the dictionaries.

* Benefits:
1- The word «طه» is nothing but two of the letters of the alphabet, and several opinions about the letters at the beginning of the sūras have already passed with us, so there is no need to repeat them. 2- Reflect, dear reader, on this music issuing from the ends of these verses, and how they all end with the alif maqṣūra, which is softer than the rest of the letters and more apt to move and to take possession; they are «لتشقى، يخشى، العلى، استوى، الثرى، أخفى، الحسنى..!» And the Qur'an is full of this music which enchants and captivates, and calls to inimitability (iʿjāz) and concision (ījāz)..!
3- The disconnected exception (al-istithnāʾ al-munqaṭiʿ): it is the exception of a thing from other than its genus; so إلا here is not for exception in the original sense, but has the meaning of لكن. Among it is His saying, Exalted is He: «ما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشى», where تذكرة is excepted from the interpreted maṣdar of تشقى, i.e. "We did not send down the Qur'an for your distress".

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الرحمن) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو" «[Note: its origin is an naʿt (adjective) of the relative noun (من), and it should by right be genitive, but it was cut off from the described for praise.. It is also possible that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause استوى.]»; (على العرش) attached to (استوى).
The clause «(هو) الرحمن ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «استوى ...» is in the position of the nominative, a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
6- (له) attached to a preposed khabar; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, a postposed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (ما) in the three places is conjoined to the first relative noun, in the position of the nominative; (في الأرض) attached to the ṣila of the second ما; (بينهما) an accusative adverb attached to the ṣila of the third ما; (تحت) an accusative adverb attached to the ṣila of the fourth ما; (الثرى) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif.
The clause «له ما في السموات ...» is in the position of the nominative, a third khabar «[Note: it may be resumptive, in which case it has no grammatical position.]»

* Morphology:
(الثرى): a noun for moist earth, on the pattern فعل with two fatḥas, and it has a weak-letter change by conversion; its origin is الثري — with a yāʾ at the end — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (بالقول) attached to (تجهر); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition, and the fāʿil (agent) of (يعلم) is a pronoun referring to Allah; (أخفى) conjoined to السرّ, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif «[Note: some permitted it to be a past verb whose object is omitted, i.e. "Allah has concealed His unseen from His servants".]». The clause «تجهر ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «إنّه يعلم ...» has no grammatical position; a causation for the implied apodosis, i.e. "if you speak aloud.. Allah is independent of that, for He knows the secret" «[Note: it is possible that the clause is the apodosis of the condition, in the position of the jussive.]».
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(أخفى): a noun of preference (ism tafḍīl) from خفي يخفى (the pattern of فرح), on the pattern أفعل, and it has a weak-letter change by conversion; its origin is أخفي; the yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) the lā of generic negation; (إله) the ism (noun) of لا, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in the omitted khabar (predicate) of لا, i.e. "there is no god existing except Him" «[Note: or it is a badal for the position of لا and its noun, and their position is the nominative.]»; (له) attached to a preposed khabar; (الأسماء) a postposed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (الحسنى) an naʿt (adjective) of الأسماء, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif.
The clause «الله لا إله إلّا هو» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «له الأسماء ...» is in the position of the nominative, a second khabar.

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (هل) a particle of interrogation to affirm the report.
The clause «أتاك حديث ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive. 10- (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (حديث); (الفاء) a conjunction; (لأهله) attached to (قال); (لعلّي) a particle resembling the verb, for hope.. and (الياء) is the ism (noun) of لعلّ, in the position of the accusative; (آتيكم) the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ.. and (كم) is a pronoun, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) «[Note: it is possible that (آتيكم) is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma.. and (كم) is a pronoun, a direct object, in the position of the accusative, and the fāʿil (agent) is أنا (I).. and the clause آتيكم is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of لعلّ.]»; (منها) attached to (آتيكم) «[Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from قبس.]»; (بقبس) attached to (آتيكم); (على النار) attached to (أجد); (هدى) a direct object, accusative «[Note: the verb أجد is transitive to one object because it has the meaning "I meet".]».
The clause «رأى ...» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause رأى.
The clause «امكثوا ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّي آنست ...» has no grammatical position; causal.
The clause «آنست نارا ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لعلّي آتيكم ...» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «أجد ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(قبس): a noun for a brand of fire, on the pattern فعل with two fatḥas.
(هدى): a maṣdar of هدى يهدي (the pattern of ضرب), and it has the meaning of a description, i.e. "guide" (hādiyan), on the pattern فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa.. and it has a weak-letter change by conversion; its origin is هدي; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

* Rhetoric:
- Arousing eagerness and urging attentive listening:
In His saying, Exalted is He, «وَهَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسى».

safi-cedvel:92-93.t:
* I'rab:
(هارون) a vocative, a single proper noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative, (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause (منعك), (إذ) an adverb, indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of an accusative, attached to (منعك).
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the vocative clause: «يا هارون ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical [Note: it is possible that the vocative clause and its response are in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said ... and the clause «ما منعك» is the response to the vocative, with no grammatical position.].
And the clause: «ما منعك ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «رأيتهم ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ضلّوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, a second direct object whose governor is (رأيتهم), i.e. "you knew them".
93- (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative, (لا) redundant (zāʾida) [Note: it is possible that (لا) is a particle of negation - not redundant - so the meaning would be: "what prevented you from not following me in anger for the sake of Allah".. and it is also possible to give (منعك) the sense of "what induced you".], (تتّبعن) it has an omitted yāʾ at its end, which is the yāʾ of the pronoun, a direct object, (الهمزة) for the interrogative of rebuke, (الفاء) a conjunction, and the sign of accusative in (أمري) is the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ..
And the interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تتّبعن..) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition attached to (منعك), i.e. "what prevented you from following me".
And the clause: «تتّبعن ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «عصيت ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause «ما منعك».

safi-cedvel:94-94.t:
* I'rab:
(ابن) a vocative muḍāf, accusative, (أمّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being the implied kasra on the mīm, because the place is occupied by the vowel suited to the omitted alif, and the omitted (الألف), which is converted from the yāʾ, is muḍāf ilayhi, (لا) a prohibitive that jusses, (بلحيتي) attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of (تأخذ) [Note: or attached to (تأخذ).], i.e. "do not seize me, holding my beard", (لا) redundant, to confirm the negation, (برأسي) attached to what (بلحيتي) is attached to, so it is conjoined to it.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تقول..) is in the position of an accusative direct object, its governor being (خشيت).
(بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (فرّقت), (بني) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being the yāʾ, for it is attached to the sound masculine plural, and (إسرائيل) is barred from tanwīn because of being a proper name and non-Arabic.. (قولي) a direct object, accusative, its sign of accusative being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يا بن أمّ ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «لا تأخذ ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «إنّي خشيت ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumptive.
And the clause: «خشيت ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «تقول ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «فرّقت ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «لم ترقب ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause (فرّقت) [Note: the yāʾ in (قولي) refers to Moses, peace be upon him, because the speech is the report of his words.. and the speech may be construed in another sense, namely that the pronoun refers to Aaron, i.e. "I feared that you would say such and such, and I feared that you would not heed my word".. so the clause is conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-type relative: (تقول).].

* Morphology:
(لحية): a rigid noun (ism jāmid), on the pattern فعلة with a kasra and a sukūn.

safi-cedvel:95-95.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) the connective of an implied conditional apodosis, (ما) an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (خطبك), (سامريّ) a vocative, a single proper noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما خطبك ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, joined with the fāʾ..
And the implied condition and its apodosis are in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said, i.e.: "If my brother has stated the truth, then what is your affair?"
And the clause: «يا سامري ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical between the two sides of the dialogue ... [Note: or resumptive.].

safi-cedvel:96-96.t:
* I'rab:
(بما) attached to (بصرت), and (ما) is a relative [Note: it is possible that it is an indefinite described noun, the clause «لم يبصروا» being in the position of a genitive, an adjective of (ما).], (به) attached to (يبصروا), (الفاء) a conjunction in both places, (قبضة) a direct object, accusative, (من أثر) attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (قبضة), and in the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from the dust of the trail of the Messenger", (الواو) resumptive, (كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute object, its governor being (سوّلت), (لي) attached to (سوّلت), and the sign of nominative in (نفسي) is the implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ.. and the (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumptive.
And the clause: «بصرت ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «لم يبصروا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «قبضت ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause (بصرت).
And the clause: «نبذتها ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause (قبضت).
And the clause: «سوّلت لي نفسي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(قبضة): it may be meant to denote the thing grasped or its quantity, in which case it is a rigid noun, and it may be meant as the maṣdar of a single act (maṣdar al-marra) from the triliteral قبض, and its pattern is فعلة with a fatḥa and a sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The story of the Sāmirī:
At the time when the appointed time for Moses' going to Mount Ṭūr arrived, Allah sent Gabriel to Moses, riding Ḥayzūm, the horse of life. The Sāmirī saw him, and wherever the horse placed its hoof it turned green and flowered. The Sāmirī said: "This horse has a special matter." So he grasped a handful of dust from the trace of where it trod. When Moses asked him about his story, he said: "I grasped a handful from the trail of the horse of the one sent to you on the day the appointed time arrived" - and perhaps he did not know that it was Gabriel. Then the Sāmirī gathered the jewellery that the Children of Israel had taken from the inhabitants of Egypt, dug a pit, kindled a fire, and left the jewellery in it; and when it melted, he made of it a calf that lowed. The Children of Israel worshipped it until Moses returned to them, and he burned it and scattered it into the sea in scattering.

safi-cedvel:97-97.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) the first is the connective of an implied conditional apodosis, and the second (الفاء) is causal, (لك) attached to an omitted khabar of inna, (في الحياة) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun of address in (لك) [Note: i.e. "in the state of your being alive".], (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative, (لا) the lā of generic negation, (مساس) the ism of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of an accusative, and the khabar of lā is omitted, i.e. "between us".
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تقول..) is in the position of an accusative, the ism of inna, placed later.
(الواو) a conjunction, (إنّ لك) like the first, (موعدا) the ism of inna, accusative, (تخلفه) an imperfect passive verb, accusative, and the (الهاء) is a direct object, and the nāʾib fāʿil is "you", (الواو) a conjunction, (إلى إلهك) attached to (انظر), (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a genitive, an adjective (naʿt) of (إلهك), and the (التاء) in (ظلت) is the ism of ẓalla, (عليه) attached to (عاكفا), which is the khabar of ẓalla, accusative, (اللام) the lām of an oath, for an implied oath, (نحرّقنّه) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of a nominative.. and the (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and the (الهاء) is a direct object, and the agent is "we", (لننسفنّه) like (لنحرقنّه), (في اليمّ) attached to (ننسفنّه), (نسفا) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «اذهب ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you disbelieve in Allah, then go" [Note: it is possible that the fāʾ links the effect to the implied cause - which is the content of what was said - i.e. Moses said "you have disbelieved in Allah, so go"; the clause «اذهب» is then conjoined to the clause «كفرت».]. And the implied conditional clause is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «إنّ لك.. أن تقول» has no grammatical position; causal.
And the clause: «تقول ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «لا مساس ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «إنّ لك موعدا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the causal clause.
And the clause: «لن تخلفه» is in the position of an accusative, an adjective of (موعدا).
And the clause: «انظر ... » is conjoined to the clause «اذهب».
And the clause: «ظلت ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «نحرّقنّه ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.. and the implied oath is resumptive.
And the clause: «ننسفنّه ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «نحرّقنّه».

* Morphology:
(مساس): a samāʿī maṣdar (one established by usage) of the quadriliteral verb ماسّ on the pattern فاعل, and the pattern of مساس is فعال with a kasra on the first letter. (نسفا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb نسف, of the pattern of ضرب, and its pattern is فعل with a fatḥa and a sukūn.

safi-cedvel:98-98.t:
* I'rab:
(الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative, an adjective (naʿt) of the sacred name (Allah), (إلّا) a particle of exception, (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative, a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in the omitted khabar, i.e. "there is no deity existing" [Note: or it is a badal for the position of (لا and its ism..), so its position is nominative.], (كلّ) a direct object, accusative, (علما) a tamyīz (specification) converted from an agent, accusative.
Clause: «إلهكم الله ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «لا إله إلّا هو ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (الذي), and the clause: «وسع ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory resumptive.

* Benefits:
- The justifications for an indefinite noun to be the owner of a ḥāl (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl). The basic rule for the owner of a ḥāl is that it be definite, because the ḥāl is a judgement by one of the attributes, so it is not permissible for the judgement to be issued upon an indefinite.
But the indefinite can obtain a justification, and become fit to be the owner of a ḥāl. The justifications are as follows:
a- When the ḥāl precedes its owner, as in: في المكتبة واقفا تلميذ (in the library, standing, is a pupil).
b- That the owner of the ḥāl is specified by an adjective, as in: «في فلك ماخر باليم مشحونا».
c- That the owner of the ḥāl is specified by annexation, as in: «في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين»; so (سواء) is a ḥāl from (أربعة) after its specification by annexation to (أيام).
d- That its owner is specified by a governed word, as in: «عجبت من ضرب أخوك شديدا».
e- That the owner of the ḥāl is specified by means of conjunction, as in: «هؤلاء جنود» وقائدهم منطلقين» [Translator's note: the quotation marks in the source are unbalanced; reproduced as written.].
And that the owner of the ḥāl is preceded by a negation, as in: «وَما أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا وَلَها كِتابٌ مَعْلُومٌ».
f- That it is preceded by a prohibition, as in:
لا يركن أحد إلى الإحجام يوم الوغى متخوفا لحمام. (Let no one incline to holding back on the day of battle, fearing death.)
g- That the owner of the ḥāl is preceded by an interrogative:
as in the saying of one of them:
يا صاح هل حمّ عيش باقيا فترى ... لنفسك العذر في ابعادها الأملا
(O my friend, has a lasting life been decreed, so that you would see for yourself an excuse in keeping hope far away?)
Here (باقيا) is a ḥāl from (عيش), and it was justified by means of the interrogative.
Sometimes the ḥāl comes from an indefinite without a justification, which is very rare, as in: «ووراءه رجال قياما» ..!

safi-cedvel:11-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لمّا) an adverb with the meaning "when" (ḥīna), containing the sense of a condition, attached to (نودي), which is a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (موسى) a single proper-noun vocative, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative.
The clause «أتاها ...» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «نودي ...» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «النداء: يا موسى ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
12- (أنا) a detached pronoun borrowed for the position of the accusative, as emphasis of the yāʾ «[Note: it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is ربّك.. and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ.. and al-ʿUkbarī permitted it to be a separator (faṣl), which is remote.]». (ربّك) the khabar of إنّ, nominative; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition, and the sign of the accusative of (نعليك) is the yāʾ; (بالواد) the khabar of إنّك, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied on the yāʾ that was dropped for lightening, in keeping with the reading in continuation (waṣl) with the yāʾ dropped because of the meeting of two silent letters; (طوى) an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — or a badal (substitute) for الوادي — genitive, its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif.
The clause «إنّي.. ربّك ...» has no grammatical position; the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اخلع ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have grasped that, then remove" «[Note: the fāʾ may be a conjunction of absolute causality, so the clause is conjoined to an implied clause caused by what precedes it, i.e. "Be alert, and remove".]».
The clause «إنّك بالوادي ...» has no grammatical position; causal.
13- (الواو) a conjunction; (أنا) a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause اخترتك; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (لما) attached to (استمع); (يوحى) an imperfect passive verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif, and the nāʾib fāʿil is "هو", which is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid).
The clause «أنا اخترتك ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اخترتك ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنا).
The clause «استمع ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have recognized your worth, then listen" «[Note: or it is conjoined by the fāʾ to an implied clause, i.e. "Be alert, and listen".]».
The clause «يوحى ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
14- 15- (إنّني أنا الله) like إنّي أنا ربّك «[Note: in verse (12) of this sūra.]»; (لا إله إلّا أنا) like لا إله إلّا هو «[Note: in verse (8) of this sūra.]»; (الفاء) connecting the effect with the cause; (لذكري) attached to (أقم); (أكاد) a defective imperfect verb — an abrogator — nominative, and its ism (noun) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا"; and the (اللام) in (لتجزى) is for causation, and (تجزى) is an imperfect passive verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif, and (كلّ) is the nāʾib fāʿil, nominative; (بما) attached to (تجزى), and ما is a maṣdar particle «[Note: and the interpreted maṣdar is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "she is recompensed with the punishment of her striving".. and it is possible that it is a relative noun with its returning pronoun omitted.]».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تجزى..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أخفيها) «[Note: or attached to the active participle آتية.]».
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تسعى) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (تجزى).
The clause «إنّني أنا الله ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption «[Note: or it is an explanation of what is revealed.]».
The clause «لا إله إلّا أنا ...» is in the position of the nominative, a second khabar of (إنّ). The clause «اعبدني ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "Be alert, and worship Me" «[Note: or it is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have believed in My lordship, worship Me".]».
The clause «أقم الصلاة ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause اعبدني.
The clause «إنّ الساعة آتية ...» has no grammatical position; causal.
The clause «أكاد أخفيها» is in the position of the nominative, a second khabar of (إنّ).
The clause «أخفيها ...» is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of أكاد. The clause «تجزى ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تسعى ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
16- (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (لا) prohibitive; (يصدّنّك) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis.. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, direct object; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, a fāʿil (agent); (لا) negative; (بها) attached to (يؤمن) and (عنها) attached to (يصدّنّك); (الفاء) the fāʾ of causality; (تردى) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif, and the fāʿil is أنت.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تردى..) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar derived from the preceding prohibition, i.e. "let there be no turning away by the one who disbelieves in the prayer, so that you perish". The clause «لا يصدّنّك ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you establish the prayer, then let not the one who does not believe in it turn you away from it". The clause «لا يؤمن بها ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (من). The clause «اتّبع ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the ṣila. The clause «تردى ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(نودي): it has a weak-letter change by conversion to suit the passive; its origin is (نادى): the first alif was converted to wāw because of the ḍamma before it, and the second alif was converted to yāʾ because of the kasra before it.
(نعليك): the singular is نعل, a rigid noun for a single piece of footwear, so it is used for the complete pair in the dual, like the word زوج.
(طوى): a proper noun with ḍamma and tanwīn — and it is read without tanwīn because of being a proper name and feminine, with the meaning of "the spot" — its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa.
(اخترتك): it has a weak-letter change by omission to suit the construction on sukūn; its origin is اختارتك with sukūn on the alif and the rāʾ; two silent letters met, so the alif was dropped.
(تردى): it has a weak-letter change by conversion; its origin is تردي — with a yāʾ at the end — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

* Benefits:
1- طوى: a proper noun for a valley in Palestine, in the lands of al-Shām, and it is a diptote; the preventer of full declension is being a proper noun and feminine, considering it a specific name of a piece of land. 2- لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى — "the preposition lām": the lām here is for causation, and it is one of the kinds of the preposition lām. «The preposition lām» has about thirty meanings; here are the most important of them.
a- Ownership: like «لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ».
b- The redundant: it is for mere emphasis, as in the saying of Ibn Mayyāda:
وملكت ما بين العراق ويثرب ... ملكا أجار لمسلم ومعاهد
(And you ruled what lies between Iraq and Yathrib — a rule that gave protection to Muslim and covenanted alike.)
هـ- The oath: like «لله لا يؤخر الأجل», i.e. تالله («By Allah, the term is not delayed»).
And wonder: like «لله درك» («To Allah belongs your goodness!»).
ز- Becoming (ṣayrūra): it is called "the lām of consequence" (lām al-ʿāqiba), like:
لدوا للموت وابنوا للخراب ... فكلكم يصير إلى ذهاب
(Give birth for death and build for ruin — for each one of you is going toward departure.)
ج- Afterness: like «أَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ» («Establish the prayer at the declining of the sun»).
ط- With the meaning of «على» (upon): like «يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقانِ», i.e. على الأذقان («they fall down upon their chins»).
ي- The lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), like «وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ». Sībawayh calls it the lām of negation, and it is preceded by a negated "to be".
«[Translator's note: the lettering of the list in the source is irregular (b, هـ, ز, ج, ط, ي, with no د or و); it is reproduced as written.]»

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is for affirmation (taqrīr); (تلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the sukūn overt on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the meeting of two silent letters, in the position of the nominative, a khabar (predicate); (بيمينك) attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) whose governor is the demonstrative.
The clause «ما تلك ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive. And the clause «يا موسى ...» has no grammatical position; parenthetical — or resumptive, to emphasize the vocative.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(عصاي) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هي), nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif.. and (الياء) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (عليها) attached to (أتوكّأ); (بها) attached to (أهشّ); (على غنمي) attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of أهشّ, i.e. "the leaves of the tree falling upon my sheep"; (الواو) a conjunction; (لي) attached to an omitted preposed khabar; (فيها) attached to the omitted khabar; (مآرب) a postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أخرى) an naʿt (adjective) of مآرب, nominative like it, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «هي عصاي ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «أتوكّأ ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption «[Note: it may be a second khabar of the pronoun هي.. and al-ʿUkbarī permitted making it a ḥāl from العصا or from the yāʾ, but the governor in it is weak.]».
The clause «أهشّ ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أتوكّأ.
The clause «لي فيها مآرب ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أتوكّأ.

* Morphology:
(مآرب): the plural of مأرب or مأربة — with fatḥa on the rāʾ of the first, and three possible vowels on the rāʾ of the second — and it is "need"; it is the noun from أرب بالشيء ("he was devoted to it") or أرب إليه ("he needed it"), the verb being of the fourth category; the pattern of مآرب is مفاعل with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
- Iṭnāb (elaboration):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «قالَ هِيَ عَصايَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا عَلَيْها وَأَهُشُّ بِها عَلى غَنَمِي», it would have sufficed to say: «هِيَ عَصايَ», but he expanded in the answer, taking delight in the address. It may also be said that this is the art of talfīf (wrapping), which is a delightful art among the arts of rhetoric. Its definition: the questioner asks about a ruling, which is one kind of a genus whose explanation — all of it or most of it — is needed; so the one asked turns away from the specific answer to what was asked, in clarifying that kind, and gives a general answer that includes the clarification of the ruling asked about and of others, because of the need to explain it. So the saying of Mūsā, in answer to the question of Allah the Exalted to him: «هِيَ عَصايَ» is the real answer to the question. Then he said «أَتَوَكَّؤُا عَلَيْها وَأَهُشُّ بِها عَلى غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيها مَآرِبُ أُخْرى», so he answered an implied question, as if he imagined that it would be said to him: And what do you do with it?
So he said, enumerating its benefits.

* Benefits:
- The staff of Mūsā.
Allah the Exalted mentioned, on the tongue of Mūsā, some of the benefits of the staff, and did not exhaust all its benefits.
The Arabs have fine speech about the "staff", and many aphorisms, which moved al-Jāḥiẓ to compose a whole book which he called «Kitāb al-ʿAṣā» (The Book of the Staff).
Abū Nuwās said concerning the people of Egypt when they rushed into sedition:
فإن يك باق إفك فرعون فيكم ... فإن عصا موسى بكفّ خصيب
(If any remnant of Pharaoh's falsehood remains among you — then the staff of Mūsā is in the hand of Khaṣīb.)
And al-Jāḥiẓ related the story of «ʿĀmir ibn al-Ẓarib», the sage of the Arabs in the Jāhiliyya, that when he grew old, and he had a daughter of such wisdom that her wisdom surpassed «Ṣaḥr bint Luqmān, Hind bint al-Ḥasan, and Khumʿa bint Ḥābis».
He used to ask his daughter, if she heard him exceed in his judgment, to strike the staff for him, so that he would turn from what he was in. And al-Ḥārith ibn Waʿla said:
وزعمتم أن لا حلوم لنا ... إن العصا قرعت لذي حلم
(And you claimed that we have no minds — yet the staff is struck for a man of mind.)
And al-Farazdaq said:
فإن كنت إنساني حلوم مجاشع ... فإن العصا كانت لذي الحلم تقرع
(If you are the pupil of the eye of Mujāshiʿ's minds — then the staff used to be struck for the man of mind.)
And al-Muḍarras al-Asadī said:
وألقت عصاها واستقر بها النوى
(She cast down her staff, and the journey's end settled for her.)
And Suwayd ibn Kurāʿ al-Kulī said:
فمن مبلغ رأس العصا ان بيننا ... ضغائن لا تنسى وان قدم الدهر
(Who will convey to the head of the staff that between us are grudges that are not forgotten, even if time grows old.)
«[Translator's note: the verse numbers of the poems are not given in the source; the glosses are brief renderings added for clarity.]»

safi-cedvel:19-20.t:
* I'rab:
(ألقها) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is أنت; (الفاء) a conjunction in both places; (إذا) of suddenness; (تسعى) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif, and the fāʿil is "هي".
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «ألقها» is in the position of the accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يا موسى ...» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
The clause «ألقاها ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «هي حيّة ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ألقاها.
The clause «تسعى» is in the position of the nominative, an naʿt (adjective) of حيّة.

* Morphology:
(حيّة): a rigid noun for the well-known animal, on the pattern فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and its ʿayn has been merged with its lām.

safi-cedvel:99-103.t:
* I'rab:
(كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute object, its governor being (نقصّ), (عليك) attached to (نقصّ), (من أنباء) attached to (نقصّ), (ما) a relative noun [Note: or an indefinite described noun, the clause after it being an adjective in the position of a genitive.] in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi, (الواو) a conjunction - or circumstantial - (من لدنّا) attached to a ḥāl from (ذكرا), which is a second direct object, accusative.
Clause: «نقصّ ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «قد سبق ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما). And the clause: «قد آتيناك ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause [Note: or in the position of an accusative ḥāl.].
100- (من) a conditional noun that jusses, indeclinable in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ, (عنه) attached to (أعرض), and the pronoun refers back to the Remembrance (al-dhikr), (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis, (يوم) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يحمل).
And the clause: «من أعرض ... » is in the position of an accusative, an adjective (naʿt) of (ذكرا).
And the clause: «أعرض عنه ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «إنّه يحمل ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
And the clause: «يحمل ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
101- (خالدين) a ḥāl from the agent of (يحمل), which refers back to the conditional (من), accusative [Note: it came in the plural form in regard to the sense of (من), after its wording had been regarded.], (فيه) attached to (خالدين), and the pronoun refers back to the punishment of the burden (al-wizr), (الواو) a conjunction, (ساء) a past verb for the formation of blame, and the agent is a latent pronoun, obligatorily so, its implied form being "هو", (لهم) attached to a ḥāl from (حملا), (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to the omitted ḥāl, (حملا) a tamyīz, accusative, specifying the pronoun in (ساء).. and the specified object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "their burden".
And the clause: «ساء لهم ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to (خالدين), and the link is implied.
102- (يوم) a badal (substitute) for (يوم القيامة), accusative like it, (في الصور) a preposition and its genitive noun, the nāʾib fāʿil, (الواو) a conjunction, (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative [Note: or indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is annexed to an indeclinable word], annexed to an indeclinable adverb, attached to (نحشر), and the tanwīn in it is the tanwīn of compensation for an omitted clause, (زرقا) a ḥāl from (المجرمين), accusative.
And the clause: «ينفخ في الصور ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «نحشر ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause (ينفخ).
103- (بينهم) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يتخافتون), (إن) negative, (إلّا) a particle of restriction, (عشرا) an adverb of time, accusative, i.e. ten nights.
And the clause: «يتخافتون ... » is in the position of an accusative, a second ḥāl from (المجرمين).
And the clause: «لبثتم ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said, for a ḥāl, i.e. "saying: you tarried only ...".

* Morphology:
(زرقا): the plural of زرقاء, feminine of أزرق, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), and its pattern is فعل with a ḍamma and a sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya):
In His words, the Exalted, «يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وِزْراً».
The word wizr originally applies to two meanings: a heavy load and sin. Its application to the punishment, with regard to the first meaning, is by way of explicit metaphor, as the punishment is likened to a heavy load; then it is borrowed for it, by the indication of the mention of the Day of Resurrection. With regard to the second meaning, it is by way of the relational trope (majāz mursal), in that the punishment is the recompense of sin, so it is concomitant with it or caused by it. The first is the more fitting with His words, the Exalted, later on (وساء) etc., because it is its ornamentation (tarshīḥ).
2- Relational trope (al-majāz al-mursal):
In His words, the Exalted, «خالِدِينَ فِيهِ».
that is, in the wizr; and one does not abide in a burden, but He meant the punishment caused by the burden, so the relation in it is causation.

* Benefits:
- لدن (ladun):
We hinted earlier at the characteristics of ladun in summary. Now we return to explain the difference between it and ʿinda. It differs from it in six matters:
a- It is bound to the starting point of ends, so the two alternate, as in: «آتَيْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا وَعَلَّمْناهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا عِلْماً», unlike "جلست عنده" (I sat at his place), where "جلست لدنه" is not permissible, for there is no sense of beginning.
b- It rarely departs from the presence of the word «من» before it..
c- It is indeclinable in the dialect of Qays, and in their dialect it was read: «من لدنه».
d- It is permissible to annex it to clauses, as we mentioned earlier.
e- It is permissible to use it on its own before «غدوة», and «غدوة» is put in the accusative after it, either as a tamyīz and direct object, or as the khabar of an omitted kāna.
And that it occurs only as an additional element (faḍla)
[Translator's note: the source text breaks off at this point, with the list incomplete (the items are lettered أ ب ج ء هـ, with a closing clause for the sixth point); it is translated as written.]

safi-cedvel:104-104.t:
* I'rab:
(بما) attached to (أعلم), and (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "they say it".], (إذ) an adverb attached to (أعلم), (طريقة) a tamyīz, accusative, (إن لبثتم إلا يوما) like (إن لبثتم إلّا عشرا) [Note: i.e. ten nights.].
Clause: «نحن أعلم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما يقولون..) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (أعلم).
And the clause: «يقول أمثلهم ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «إن لبثتم إلّا ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.

* Morphology:
(أمثلهم): an elative (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral مثل يمثل, of the pattern of كرم, in the sense of "he excelled", on the pattern أفعل. It came in the singular because it is annexed to a definite noun, although the pronoun in it refers to a plurality; this is permissible, just as it is permissible to put it in the plural, agreeing with the preceding plural.

safi-cedvel:105-107.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (عن الجبال) attached to (يسألونك), (الفاء) the connective of an implied conditional apodosis, and the sign of nominative in (ربّي) is the implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ, (نسفا) an absolute object, accusative, (الفاء) a conjunction, and the pronoun in (يذرها) refers back to the mountains or their foundations levelled with the earth, (قاعا) an accusative ḥāl from the third-person pronoun (in يذرها) [Note: or a second direct object, if (يذر) is counted among the verbs of becoming.], (صفصفا) a second accusative ḥāl [Note: or a badal (substitute) for (قاعا), because it has its meaning.].
Clause: «يسألونك ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «قل ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you answer, then say".
And the clause: «ينسفها ربّي ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said.
And the clause: «يذرها ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause «ينسفها».
107- (فيها) attached to (ترى), (لا) the second is redundant, to confirm the negation, (أمتا) conjoined to (عوجا) by the wāw, accusative.
And the clause: «لا ترى ... » is in the position of an accusative, a third ḥāl from the hāʾ in (يذرها) [Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(قاعا): a name for soft, level ground, on the pattern فعل with two fatḥas; its plural is أقواع, أقوع (with a fatḥa on the hamza and a ḍamma on the wāw), قيع, قيعان and قيعة. In القاع there is an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is القوع, the wāw having a vowel after a fatḥa was changed to an alif.
(صفصفا): a name for level, smooth ground, on the pattern فعلل, with a fatḥa on the first fāʾ and the first lām.
(أمتا): a name for a protrusion and a raised place or a hill; its plural is آمات and أموت, and the pattern of أمت is فعل with a fatḥa and a sukūn.

* Benefits:
